title: The basic vowels
subtitle: ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ
review: Written by Claude. The Korean and the romanization have not been checked by a Korean speaker. No audio yet: the Korean voice is not chosen.
intro: Korean has more vowel sounds than English letters can show. Start with these: each one is short and steady, and each has its own Hangul letter.

groups.title: Six simple vowels
notes: Each vowel is one steady sound. It does not slide into another sound, as English vowels often do.
In Hangul a vowel on its own is written with a silent ㅇ in front of it: 아, 어, 오.

words.en: as in son, with the mouth open and the lips relaxed
as in more, with round lips
like u, but with the lips spread, not round

groups.title: Two more: ae and e
notes: Today most speakers say these two the same way, like the e in pet. The spelling still tells them apart.

groups.title: Vowels in words
notes: When two vowels meet, say each one clearly: a-i, o-i, u-yu.
A y in front gives ya, yeo, yo, yu. In Hangul that is one more short stroke: ㅑ ㅕ ㅛ ㅠ.
